^The employee hesitates at first, a little pinprick in the back of their mind begging them to walk further into the chamber.
^When that one pinprick turns into a hundred more, they finally succumb.
^The employee allows themselves to become sustenance for the perfect lifeform.
^Mitosis Rabbit seems tempted to make a meal out of the employee at first. In fact, it even tries to take a few bites.
^However, upon realizing that the employee has come bearing heaps of sustenance, that anger quickly fades.
^Its purpose restored, it makes the fullest use of every single morsel. For a moment, it's easy to forget that it's even a Mortem.
^However, when it follows this up by rapidly dividing into a copy of itself, the employee returns to reality.
^Today, the employee gives Mitosis Rabbit an extra helping of food.
^It absorbs every last crumb directly into its body, quickly dissolving away into nothingness.
^When the employee has finished giving Mitosis Rabbit its much needed affection, the moment their back is turned, its body writhes and splits.
^Even so, Mitosis Rabbit doesn't seem to appreciate the gesture.
^The employee sets aside one of the Mitosis Rabbits. Whether it was the original or not doesn't matter.
^With a heaping dose of salt, the others are quickly removed from this world, their bodies shrivelling up as they expell their contents.
^The copies try their hardest to tear the employee to shreds in response, fighting for their lives. It hurts like hell.
^Despite everything, as all of this is unfolding, the last one doesn't seem to respond at all.
^It's not going to be culled, of course. Why should it care?

^When everything is over, the hoard is dispatched, and the last remaining Mitosis Rabbit happily absorbs the spilt blood.

ResearchEvent: ^The employee sets aside one of the rabbits and retrieves the salt, as usual.
^Normally, whenever Mitosis Rabbit's numbers need to be culled, the lone member doesn't react at all to the massacre of its offspring.
^This time however, just before the culling starts, it bumps up against the employee's leg to get their attention.
^This Mortem is incapable of speech, but its expressions are enough to inuit some meaning.
^It gives the employee a quizzical glance.
^"Why does this have to be done?" it seems to ask. "Have I done something wrong?"
^The employee has a chance to respond.
ResearchNothing: ^The rabbit's glance only seems to grow more puzzled.
^"I don't understand," it seems to suggest. "If there's nothing wrong about what I'm doing, why do you want to stop it?"
ResearchDontWant: ^"Then this all seems quite silly," the rabbit thinks.
^"If you don't want this, then it would be much better to help instead. Wouldn't it?"
^There's a sudden, overwhelming psychic pressure that overtakes the employee.
^Every single nerve in their body suddenly urges them to submit themselves as nothing more than sustenance to a far more deserving creature.
ResearchTooEfficient: ^"Too efficient?" the rabbit ponders. "All I'm doing is living."
^"Perhaps you fear me so much that by simply being alive, you think I am a threat to you."
^Before the employee can respond, Mitosis Rabbit hops off, giving the employee one more look.
^"I suppose this is your one way of keeping yourselves safe."
^"Safe from something so much better at living than you."
^It goes back to its usual demeanor, not reacting at all as its bretheren are killed.
^A greater understanding of Mitosis Rabbit has been acquired.
ResearchSilent2: ^The rabbit waits for a response, but receives none. That, to it, seems to be all the response it needs.
^"If you don't want this, then it would be much better to help instead. Wouldn't it?"
^There's a sudden, overwhelming psychic pressure that overtakes the employee.

ResearchExist: ^The rabbit's ears fold down, its eyes expressing a modicum of sadness.
^"That seems quite cruel," its demeanor suggests. "I'm only doing exactly what you humans do."
^"Correct. It's the fact that you're too efficient at it."
ResearchDenial: ^"But I most certainly am!" it thumps. "I eat like you. I breed like you. The only difference is that I'm faster than you."
^Mitosis Rabbit sizes up the employee, its eyes dialating with hunger and frustration.
^"If this is what you humans believe, perhaps I should prove them wrong."
^Without warning, Mitosis Rabbit lunges for the employee's neck.
ResearchSilent3: ^The rabbit waits for a response, but receives none. It seems frustrated by this.
^"How strange," it conveys. "Perhaps you humans don't like it when something else can live just as well as you do."
^Mitosis Rabbit hops off. It goes back to its usual demeanor, not reacting at all as its bretheren are killed.
^A breakthrough seems to be in sight, but has not yet been reached.
ResearchCare: ^The rabbit seems to think on this for a moment. Although this would be simple for a human to answer, the logic doesn't seem to compute for Mitosis Rabbit.
^It looks to its copies, conveying the idea of "Because one day, it could be me among those getting culled."
^"I don't really want to die. It means there can't be anymore of me. And that would be bad."
ResearchWhyBad: ^"Because then I stop living. The whole point of life is to live."
^As Mitosis Rabbit seems to realize its incongruous logic, it hops off, awaiting the culling of its fellow members.
^"Maybe there is no difference between life and death for you humans."
^It goes back to its usual demeanor, not reacting at all as its bretheren are killed.
^A greater understanding of Mitosis Rabbit has been acquired.
ResearchEnough: ^It tilts its head. "Enough?" it seems to question.
^"But there's no such thing. My whole purpose is to make more of me."
ResearchYes: ^"Then I see no reason why I shouldn't try and fight against this."
^"If you die, that means I keep living, right?"
^Without warning, Mitosis Rabbit lunges for the employee's neck.

^"Maybe if you lived like me, you would understand."
^It goes back to its usual demeanor, not reacting at all as its bretheren are killed.
